newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stock futures trade for first time in 11 months. [CORRECTED 11:31 GMT]
newsitem.headline: HK stock futures trade for first time in 11 months. [CORRECTED 11:31 GMT]

text.p: The Hong Kong Futures Exchange (HKFE) said on Friday it has registered its first trading activity in stock futures in nearly a year after launching an automated trading system for the shunned product.
"Stock futures have generated renewed interest today as they moved into the new trading environment provided by the Hong Kong Futures Exchange," the HKFE said in a statement.

The Exchange moved trading in the stock futures -- available for only three blue-chip stocks -- to the automated system from an open outcry environment on Friday to provide liquidity. Timber Hill Hong Kong Ltd was commissioned as a market maker.
Twenty-three HSBC Holdings Ltd contracts traded on Friday, as well as five (corrects from seven) Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd contracts and five Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd contracts.
"We at HKFE are pleased with the positive response from the market and we look forward to continued growth of this product," HKFE chief executive office Ivers Riley said.
Ross Lai, HKFE senior manager, public affairs and marketing, said it was the first time trading was registered in the contracts since March 1996.
"It is not that glamorous but it is showing signs of revival," he said.
One futures trader said the impact had really not been significant.
"There is some small trading in the market. I think people are just testing the system," she said.
